issue_context.title: Replace reflect.DeepEqual with cmp.Diff in pkg/scheduler tests
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

In some tests, `reflect.DeepEqual` is used to compare expected and actual values. It should be replaced to `cmp.Diff` if possible.

### Why is this needed?

According to the [SIG Scheduling guidelines](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/sig-scheduling/CONTRIBUTING.md#technical-and-style-guidelines), `cmp.Diff` should be used instead of `reflect.DeepEqual`.

review_comments: schedulerCmpOpts does not have IgnoreFields, do you mean it wasn't needed?
I think it might have been introduced by mistake - perhaps author's original intention was to allow unexported fields? Either way, comparisons pass for NodeStatus as well
we don't have to declare it if it's only used at one place

True. I added it for easier maintainability, so that all tests in pkg/scheduler look similarly.
I'm new to Go and it took me a while to understand all the "field unexported" errors I got when introducing cmp.Diff, I thought that declaring this var could draw the attention of the next person adding tests here, and maybe save them a bit of time

For framework.Status comparison, can we use ↓ instead of cmp.diff?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L386-L402

Please see discussion with @macsko here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129905/files/8090ea9d67a09b290de31efafabcdf96619c6b05#diff-37ad603da4c20f50731d7b563fad3768f6dfbc146e38fcb573393081b2ba8488R1007
TL;DR; We can't because the Equal function fails comparing error objects here (since they are not the exact same object). This tests needs refactoring to fix this and I'll be happy to do it, but I strongly feel this is out of scope of this PR.
I think it could, but it seems that it would decrease readability significantly. If you don't have a strong opinion here, I'll leave the current comparer function
+1 for @dom4ha 's suggestion since that would allow us to remove `.sort()` function.
I agree with @ania-borowiec that it can't be done easily.
